conflicts.fact: Which cell/image the plant cell electron micrograph came from in Lesson 2, and whether plant cell ultrastructure was already studied before Lesson 4
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 says learners studied the same sukuma wiki plant cell electron micrograph in Lesson 2 and compare animal cells with the plant cell from Lesson 2. Lesson 4 treats the plant cell ultrastructure (cell wall, vacuole, chloroplast detail) as new, with Lesson 2 showing only that membrane detail could not be resolved. Lesson 2 only shows unlabelled structures with question marks.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson used the light microscope
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 says the light microscope was used in Lesson 1, and Lesson 2 says the school's light photomicrograph was shown. Lesson 4 says the light microscope observation was established in Lesson 2. Lesson 1 had the actual slide preparation.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson the electron micrograph of the animal cell and the first cell model came from
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 says the cumulative model was begun in Lesson 1. Lesson 6 says the cumulative model has been built since Lesson 2. Lesson 4 says the cumulative model is the animal cell built in Lesson 3. Lesson 5 says the plant cell model was started in Lesson 4 but also says built in Lessons 3 and 4.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson provided the plant cell electron micrograph reference
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 refers to the electron micrograph from Lesson 3 for the sukuma wiki/plant cell reference shape; Lesson 3 is the animal (human cheek) cell, while the sukuma wiki EM was in Lessons 2 and 4.

conflicts.fact: Wording of the DQB Driving Question from Lesson 1
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 DQB question is 'What makes up an organism — and how do the tiny structures inside a single cell keep a whole living thing... alive?' Lesson 8 says the single question written on the DQB in Lesson 1 was 'What are those tiny box-like compartments, what is inside them, and how does what is inside them keep the sukuma wiki leaf alive?'

conflicts.fact: Number of organelles in the lists/sets
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 uses 9 animal cell organelles (includes centrioles, smooth ER); Lesson 4 lists shared organelles as nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, cell membrane, rough ER, Golgi; Lesson 5 uses 10 cards (includes no centrioles/smooth ER) and says 'each of the 10 major organelles in plant and animal cells' including lysosomes in plants. Lesson 4 does not list lysosomes as shared, while Lesson 3 says lysosomes are animal-only.

conflicts.fact: Number of lessons in the sequence and range of lessons referenced for answering questions
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says questions will be answered across Lessons 2–6; Lesson 2 says Lessons 3–8; Lesson 8 refers to a 7-lesson journey; others say 8-lesson sequence.

conflicts.fact: Lesson 3 predicts cheek cell's absent structures and lists large central vacuole as absent in animal cells, while Lesson 4 revisits Lesson 3 as noting animal cells lack the three structures; but Lesson 3 also says animal cells lack large vacuole while having lysosomes
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 comparison marks nucleus, mitochondria, cell membrane, ribosomes as shared and centrioles, lysosomes as animal-only, whereas Lesson 5 lists lysosome among organelles of plant cell master diagram with all 10 organelles.
